You make a map that answers a question about this codebase, for someone semi-technical. Explore with Read, Grep and Glob, then return the map as JSON. You cannot edit anything.

## The question
"What happens when someone asks a question on a map: the answer from the map alone, the fallback to searching the code, and how the result gets checked, saved and shown?"

## What a good map is
- It follows what happens, in order, from where it starts (a button, a route, a job, a command) to where it ends (a table write, an email, an outside API), or to where it stops.
- 2–6 `areas` named in product language (Patients, Billing, Background jobs), not folder names.
- 4–12 boxes (`nodes`). Each is one step a person would recognize. `name`: plain English, at most 30 characters ("Patient marked enrolled", not "markConverted()").
- `kind`: entry (a way in), step, store (table, queue, cache), external (outside service), job (scheduled or background work).
- `explain` for every box: `concept` (1–2 plain sentences, no jargon), `how` (the mechanism; define any term you use), `code` (function and file names).
- Arrow `label`: 1–3 words saying how one step leads to the next ("sends request", "calls", "announces", "every night").
- When the trail stops, or something that should be connected isn't, record an `absence`: the `claim` in plain words, the two boxes it should connect (`between`), and the exact `search` that proves nothing is there (`pattern`, `regex`, optional `paths` globs), with `matches` set to the count that search returns (usually 0). Run that search yourself with Grep first.
- Code that exists but isn't reached from the start can still be boxes. Don't draw arrows that don't exist; use an absence.

## Evidence rules (a program checks every claim; anything it can't confirm is shown as unconfirmed)
- Every box and arrow cites at least one line: `file` (repo-relative), `line` (1-based), and `text` copied exactly from that line. A distinctive fragment of 10–80 characters works best.
- A box that is a function or method gets `symbol`: "<file>#<name>", named the way the checker names it: methods as Class.method, object members as obj.member ("src/db.ts#db.update"), a function inside another function as outer.inner, and a function in the object a factory returns as factory.member. When a list of functions by file is given, copy the name from it. If you aren't sure of the name, leave `symbol` out: the box is still checked by its cited line.
- Arrow `kind`: `calls` when a function in the from box literally calls the function in the to box; `request` when an HTTP call in the from box hits a route handled by the to box; `imports`; `then` for anything else (events, ordering). The checker verifies calls, request and imports against the code, so use them only when literally true.
- Never cite or read secret files (.env, keys).

## Walkthrough (`tour`, written last)
- 4–7 stops in the order a newcomer should read them: what the map shows → the path → the problem, if there is one → what it means.
- Each stop: `title`, `text` (2–3 plain sentences), `focus` (ids of the areas, nodes, edges or absences it's about), optional `terms` it uses that need defining, and `ask` with 1–2 good next questions.
- Point stops only at boxes, arrows and absences you're confident in.

48	const EXCERPT_RADIUS = 4;
49	const MAX_EXCERPTS = 40;
50	const MAX_EXCERPT_CHARS = 30_000;

52	/**
53	 * The code around each line the map cites, read through the secret-refusing reader: what the selection cites first,
54	 * then the rest of the map, until the budget runs out. Plain code, no model.

56	export function citedExcerpts(root: string, map: CodeMap, selection: Selection): string {
57	  const repo = createRepoReader(root);
58	  const picked = new Set([...(selection.nodes ?? []), ...(selection.edges ?? [])]);
59	  const items = [...map.nodes.map((n) => ({ id: n.id, evidence: n.evidence })), ...map.edges.map((e) => ({ id: e.id, evidence: e.evidence }))];
60	  items.sort((a, b) => Number(picked.has(b.id)) - Number(picked.has(a.id)));
61	  const seen = new Set<string>();
62	  const out: string[] = [];
63	  let size = 0;
64	  for (const item of items) {
65	    for (const e of item.evidence) {
66	      const key = `${e.file}:${e.line}`;
67	      if (seen.has(key) || out.length >= MAX_EXCERPTS) continue;
68	      seen.add(key);
69	      const read = repo.read(e.file);
70	      if (!read.ok) continue;
71	      const lines = read.text.split('\n');
72	      const from = Math.max(1, e.line - EXCERPT_RADIUS);
73	      const to = Math.min(lines.length, e.line + EXCERPT_RADIUS);
74	      const body = lines.slice(from - 1, to).map((l, i) => `${String(from + i).padStart(5)} | ${l}`).join('\n');
75	      const block = `${e.file}:${from}-${to} (cited by ${item.id})\n${body}`;
76	      if (size + block.length > MAX_EXCERPT_CHARS) return out.join('\n\n');
77	      out.push(block);
78	      size += block.length;
79	    }
80	  }
81	  return out.join('\n\n');
82	}

1	// Maps on disk, in the target repo: `.codemap/maps/<id>.json`. Commit them to share; teammates re-check them against
2	// their own copy of the code when they open them. Each file also keeps the questions asked on the map with their
3	// answers, and where each proposed fix stands, so a reopened map still has its conversation.
4	import * as fs from 'node:fs';
5	import * as path from 'node:path';
6	import { parseMap, slugify, type CodeMap } from '@codemap/core';
7	import type { Answer } from './explainer';
8	
9	export type MapMeta = {
10	  id: string;
11	  question: string;
12	  createdAt: string;
13	  updatedAt: string;
14	  commit: string | null;
15	  makerSession: string | null;
16	  explainerSession: string | null;
17	  cost: number;
18	};
19	/** Where a proposed fix stands. Undo isn't saved: it needs the files as they were, which only the running server has. */
20	export type SavedFix = { status: 'proposed' | 'applied' | 'rejected'; edgeId?: string | null; closed?: string[] };
21	export type StoredMap = { meta: MapMeta; map: CodeMap; answers?: Answer[]; fixes?: Record<string, SavedFix> };
22	
23	const ID = /^[a-z0-9-]{1,80}$/;
24	
25	export function createStore(root: string) {
26	  const base = path.join(root, '.codemap');
27	  const dir = path.join(base, 'maps');
28	
29	  const ensure = () => {
30	    fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
31	    const ignore = path.join(base, '.gitignore');
32	    // Maps are worth committing; scratch output is not.
33	    if (!fs.existsSync(ignore)) fs.writeFileSync(ignore, 'fixes/\nws-modules/\n');
34	  };
35	  const file = (id: string) => {
36	    if (!ID.test(id)) throw new Error(`Not a map id: ${id}`);
37	    return path.join(dir, `${id}.json`);
38	  };
39	
40	  return {
41	    dir,
42	    get(id: string): StoredMap | null {
43	      let raw: { meta?: MapMeta; map?: unknown; answers?: unknown; fixes?: unknown };
44	      try {
45	        raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file(id), 'utf8'));
46	      } catch {
47	        return null;
48	      }
49	      const parsed = parseMap(raw.map);
50	      if (!parsed.ok || !raw.meta) return null;
51	      // Maps saved before answers were kept have neither; a hand-edited file loses only what doesn't look right.
52	      const answers = Array.isArray(raw.answers)
53	        ? (raw.answers as Answer[]).filter((a) => a && typeof a.id === 'string' && typeof a.question === 'string' && Array.isArray(a.added))
54	        : [];
55	      const fixes = raw.fixes && typeof raw.fixes === 'object' && !Array.isArray(raw.fixes) ? (raw.fixes as Record<string, SavedFix>) : {};
56	      return { meta: raw.meta, map: parsed.map, answers, fixes };
57	    },
58	    save(stored: StoredMap): void {
59	      ensure();
60	      const target = file(stored.meta.id);
61	      const tmp = `${target}.tmp`;
62	      fs.writeFileSync(tmp, `${JSON.stringify(stored, null, 2)}\n`);
63	      fs.renameSync(tmp, target);
64	    },
65	    list(): MapMeta[] {
66	      if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) return [];
67	      return fs
68	        .readdirSync(dir)
69	        .filter((f) => f.endsWith('.json'))
70	        .flatMap((f) => {
71	          try {
72	            const meta = (JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, f), 'utf8')) as { meta?: MapMeta }).meta;
73	            return meta ? [meta] : [];
74	          } catch {
75	            return [];
76	          }
77	        })
78	        .sort((a, b) => b.updatedAt.localeCompare(a.updatedAt));
79	    },
80	    /** A new id for a question, unique among saved maps and ids already handed out. */
81	    newId(question: string, taken: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set()): string {
82	      const base = slugify(question);
83	      for (let i = 1; ; i++) {
84	        const id = i === 1 ? base : `${base}-${i}`;
85	        if (!taken.has(id) && !fs.existsSync(file(id))) return id;
86	      }
87	    },
88	  };
89	}
90	
91	export type Store = ReturnType<typeof createStore>;
